newsitem.title: UK: Taleban lose hundreds killed in Afghanistan-agency.
newsitem.headline: Taleban lose hundreds killed in Afghanistan-agency.

text.p: Hundreds of Taleban fighters were killed and 400 captured when the Afghan Islamic militia were driven out of the town of Charikar, north of Kabul, the Iranian news agency IRNA reported, quoting Afghan officials in Teheran.
The agency said a statement on Sunday by the Afghan embassy in the Iranian capital had announced that forces loyal to the government had retaken the city.
The statement said the key town of Jabal os-Siraj, to the north of Charikar, had also been recaptured and some Taleban fighters had been trapped during their retreat.
Reuters reported earlier from Kabul, quoting reliable sources, that former Afghan government military chief Ahmad Shah Masood had rolled back the Taleban and taken the two towns.
The hardline Taleban drove Masood out of Kabul two weeks ago and have since been imposing a strict Islamic rule.
The Taleban had set up a front-line headquarters at Jabal os-Siraj, which lies a two-hour drive from Kabul at the mouth of the Salang Pass that leads through the Hindu Kush mountains.
Reuters quoted the sources as saying Masood took Jabal os-Siraj and then captured Charikar, a 30-minute drive south, after a fierce five-hour battle.
